name: apc_classic_ac
description: Cross-process APC injection (MITRE T1055.004) against AssaultCube (32-bit ac_client.exe). Attacker opens the target, allocates a small RWX page, writes a 10-byte __stdcall shellcode that atomically increments a hit counter, then calls QueueUserAPC to schedule that shellcode on ac_client.exe's main thread. Unlike apc_classic (which targets TestTarget's SleepEx(TRUE)-alertable main loop), AC's main thread only ever hits non-alertable waits (SDL 1.2 uses plain Sleep for frame limiting), so the APC queues but never drains during the observation window. The install-time ETW-TI event (KERNEL_THREATINT_TASK_QUEUEUSERAPC) fires regardless — this is the point: even against a target whose payload never executes, the injection attempt is detectable at the kernel level. Runtime firing is deliberately not checked (--verify-hits 0).

extra.verify_hits_rationale: AC's main thread uses non-alertable waits (SDL 1.2 Sleep, PeekMessage), so a queued APC never drains during the observation window. This is a real limitation of user-mode APC injection against game loops that don't opt into alertable waits — and precisely why the Early-Bird variant exists (queue the APC pre-main() when NtTestAlert would drain it). For this baseline, we measure install-detectability only.
extra.expected_fingerprint: 1x cross-process OpenProcess (attacker → ac_client.exe with hostile mask), 1x cross-process OpenThread, 1x ALLOCVM_REMOTE (RWX trampoline, ~4KB), 1x WRITEVM_REMOTE (shellcode+counter, 4KB write), 1x KERNEL_THREATINT_TASK_QUEUEUSERAPC. Notably absent: 0x THREAD_CREATE_REMOTE, 0x SETTHREADCONTEXT.
